options.text: Graphite is an element because it is a pure substance made of only one kind of identical particle.
Chlorine gas is an element because it is a pure substance made of only one kind of identical particle.
Table salt is an element because the crystals look uniform and pure.
Rust powder is an element because it is a solid powder used in the lab.

stem:
Krish studies four pure samples in the lab: graphite made of only carbon particles; table salt made of particles that each contain sodium and chlorine joined together; chlorine gas made of identical molecules that each contain only chlorine; and rust powder made of particles that each contain iron and oxygen joined together.

Which claims correctly classify a substance as an element? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: An element is a pure substance of one kind of particle. Graphite (carbon) and chlorine fit that; salt and rust each join more than one element and are compounds. Looking uniform or being a solid powder is not the test.
